SCOPE OF THIS SLICE: add a `module` grouping to the NavItem shape and render the sidebar grouped under the six module headings; all current hrefs (e.g. /plan, /plan/schedule, /lessons, /growth, /attendance, /records, /settings?tab=children) stay exactly as they are. Changing the NavItem type touches all navConfig consumers — Sidebar.tsx, isNavItemActive(), validateNavConfig() and their tests — so the build must pass. NOTE: this workstream and the rewritten 'portfolio grade-discoverability' workstream both edit features/layout/lib/navConfig.ts — this one adds a `module` key to every NavItem (including 'grades-progress'); land it FIRST, then the grade-discoverability label rename is applied on top in the same branch (see that workstream's blastRadiusNotes for the explicit sequencing).

workstreams.blastRadiusNotes:
The audit confirmed the suspicion in the original note: AttendanceSummary already aggregates and displays per-learner totals end-to-end — there is no missing capability. The feedback is a labeling/discoverability gap (the heading doesn't name which learner the totals belong to), fixable as a tiny, contained, auto-eligible change (Mode 1 — pure UI labeling, zero data-layer touch). Add a visible label naming the selected learner above/alongside (e.g.

Summary — {selectedChild?.name}

), resolved via children.find(c => c.id === selectedChildId) (the page already has `children` in scope from useHousehold()). Optionally pass the resolved name into AttendanceSummary as an optional `learnerName` prop so its empty-state copy can name the learner too. No schema, repository, service, or route change — the type, contract, and aggregation are already correctly per-learner at every layer. Full findings in docs/bug_enhancement/20260606-attendance-totals-plan.md.

testPlan: UPDATE TEST: features/layout/__tests__/navConfig.test.ts — read the existing assertions first to avoid duplicating one, then add/update an assertion that the 'grades-progress' nav item's label no longer contains the word 'Grades' (regression-proof against re-promising a feature that doesn't exist), while its href ('/growth') and activePrefixes (['/growth', '/portfolio']) remain unchanged
workstreams.blastRadiusNotes:
The audit found this is not a discoverability gap but a missing-feature request mislabeled as one — an exhaustive grep across portfolio, plan, subjects, and records features found zero grade-input surfaces anywhere in the codebase (no field, type, status value, or form input stores a numeric/letter score for student work). The contained fix (Mode 1 — pure copy/IA, one string-literal edit) is retitling the misleading nav label at features/layout/lib/navConfig.ts:38 from 'Grades & Progress' to something that matches what the destination actually offers (e.g. 'Growth' / 'Growth & Reflection', aligning with PortfolioPage.tsx's own

Growth

heading) — no routing, type, schema, service, or repository change. CONFLICT WITH THE NAVIGATION WORKSTREAM (WS3, feedback e1c3f3db, same branch): both workstreams edit the SAME 'grades-progress' object literal in features/layout/lib/navConfig.ts — WS3 adds a `module` grouping key to every NavItem (including this one) without touching any label/href, while this workstream edits only that entry's `label` string. APPLY THIS RENAME AFTER WS3's module-grouping change lands in the same branch: rebase onto WS3's commit, change only the `label` field on the existing 'grades-progress' item, and do NOT revert or alter the `module` key WS3 added. Re-run features/layout/__tests__/navConfig.test.ts and features/layout/__tests__/Sidebar.test.tsx together once both edits coexist. The underlying capability ('let a parent record an assignment grade') is a separate, schema-touching follow-up plan and is explicitly out of scope here — do not add a placeholder grade field anywhere. Full findings in docs/bug_enhancement/20260606-grade-discoverability-plan.md.

workstreams.summary: BUG (not in the feedback queue) — On /portfolio the Subject dropdown cannot be used even though the learner has subjects. Trace where PortfolioPage sources its subject list and which id it carries (Workspace id vs HouseholdProfile/StudentProfile id), confirm it matches the child id used in the dropdown, and fix the mismatch (or loading/scoping gap) so a learner's subjects are selectable.

workstreams.blastRadiusNotes: Root cause unverified — most likely an id-boundary mismatch (subject.childId vs the selected child id; per project rules householdId on students is HouseholdProfile.id, not Workspace.id).
